# Appeal of Denial – Cervical Fusion (ACDF), CPT 22551

**RE: Request for Reconsideration of Adverse Benefit Determination**
**Member:** Rowan Delgado
**Member ID:** W865123628
**Reference Number:** POC-9391F374E1-41425
**Date of Denial Notice:** 2026-08-18
**Governing Policy:** Cervical Fusions, S-9004-02 — https://www.bcbsnd.com/providers/policies-precertification/legacy-medical-policy/c/cervical-fusions (effective 2024-07-01)

Dear Blue Cross Blue Shield of North Dakota Appeals Department,

I am appealing the denial of my prior authorization request for a cervical fusion (ACDF), CPT code 22551, which was denied on 2026-08-18 as not medically necessary. My surgeon, Dr. Marchetti, has documented that this procedure is needed, and I believe the records already in my file show that I meet the plan's own published criteria for this surgery.

## The Plan's Own Criteria and How My Records Meet Them

The plan's policy, Cervical Fusions, S-9004-02, states:

> "ACDF) is considered medically necessary for treatment of symptomatic degenerative disease when ALL of the following criteria are met:"

The policy then lists the required elements. Below, I map each one to what is already documented in my chart.

**1. Radiculopathy/myelopathy refractory to at least six weeks of conservative treatment, without progressive or severe myelopathy.** The policy states:

> "unremitting cervical radiculopathy and/or myelopathy (i.e., neck and arm pain) resulting in disability and/or neurological deficit that are refractory to at least six weeks of standard conservative, nonoperative management (e.g., reduced activities, exercise, analgesics, physical therapy), in the absence of progressive or severe myelopathy"

My records show 14 months of progressive neck pain, with radicular pain, numbness, and weakness extending into my right thumb and index finger. I completed 8 weeks (18 visits) of supervised physical therapy, including cervical traction and postural training, from 2026-05-18 to 2026-07-13 — longer than the six weeks the policy requires. I also used NSAIDs for 8 months with inadequate relief and received a corticosteroid injection on 2026-05-08 that gave only 3 weeks of partial relief. My exam findings show a neurologic deficit corresponding to the imaged level, and there is no documentation of progressive or severe myelopathy.

**2. Imaging demonstrating a qualifying finding at the affected level.** The policy states:

> "complex imaging studies (i.e., CT, MRI, X-ray) demonstrate at least ONE of the following at each impacted level being considered for the fusion:"

and lists, among other findings:

> "Herniated nucleus pulposus"

My MRI of the cervical spine dated 2026-06-26 shows a C5-C6 disc herniation with severe right foraminal narrowing and C6 nerve root compression.

**3. Correlation between physical exam and imaging findings at the level being fused.** The policy states:

> "physical examination findings and imaging studies correlate with each level being considered for the fusion"

My exam findings — positive provocative testing on the right side and a neurologic deficit matching the C6 distribution — correlate directly with the C5-C6 finding on my MRI.

Taken together, my clinical records appear to satisfy each of the elements the plan's own policy requires for ACDF to be considered medically necessary.

## Request for the Criteria Applied to My Case

Blue Cross Blue Shield of North Dakota writes and publishes its own medical necessity criteria for this procedure. I am requesting that the plan provide, in writing, the specific criteria it applied in reviewing my request, along with an explanation of which criterion or criteria it found my records did not meet. If the plan relied on any criteria other than those in Cervical Fusions, S-9004-02, I ask that those be identified and provided to me as well.

## Closing Request

I respectfully ask that Blue Cross Blue Shield of North Dakota reconsider this denial and approve coverage for the ACDF procedure recommended by my surgeon, based on the medical necessity criteria in the plan's own policy and the records described above. My appeal must be received by 2027-02-14. I understand I should send this appeal to the address printed on my denial letter, or I can call the number on the back of my insurance card to confirm where member appeals are filed.

Please let me know if any additional information is needed to complete this review. Thank you for your time and reconsideration.

Sincerely,

[Signature]
Rowan Delgado
Member ID: W865123628
[Address]
[Phone number]
[Email address]
Date: [date]

---

*This letter is not medical or legal advice and does not guarantee that coverage will be approved.*
